title: Eritrea vs. South Africa: Decisive Clash in AFCON 2027 Qualifiers
seoTitle: Eritrea vs. South Africa: Decisive AFCON 2027 Qualifier
subtitle: The match marks the first official encounter between the national teams and could decide qualification for the final phase.
excerpt: In the second round of the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, Eritrea and South Africa face off at Al Salam Stadium in Cairo.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Eritrea and South Africa, scheduled for September 30th at 1 PM at Al Salam Stadium in Cairo, is the first official encounter between the two national teams. The match carries extra weight because Group D offers only one direct spot for the final phase of the Africa Cup of Nations 2027, as Kenya automatically qualifies as the host nation.

Group D Context

  • South Africa leads with three points after defeating Guinea in the opening round.
  • Eritrea has one point after a 1-1 draw with Kenya, keeping their chances of advancing in the group alive.
  • The match could determine who takes the lead and who will contend for the spot at home.

Head-to-Head History

This game marks the first official contact between Eritrea and South Africa, whether in official competitions or friendlies. It will be South Africa's 50th different African opponent since their readmission in 1992, highlighting the journey of South African football's reintegration into the continental scene.

Team Preparations

South Africa arrives at the match with a squad that includes 13 players from Mamelodi Sundowns, in addition to athletes in European leagues such as Relebohile Mofokeng (Union Saint-Gilloise) and Thapelo Maseko (Copenhagen). Coach Pitso Mosimane, who managed Al Ahly in matches at Al Salam Stadium, is well-acquainted with the arena and could use this familiarity to his advantage.

Eritrea, in turn, rebuilt its squad after the desertion crisis in March 2026. The team features 14 international debutants recruited from clubs in 13 different countries, including Australia, Egypt, England, Germany, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, the Philippines, and Romania. Captain Ablelom Teklezghi, midfielder Nahom Tadese, and forward Romel Abdu are the few remaining domestic players.

Tactical Strategies

Mosimane typically employs a 4-3-3 formation focusing on defensive solidity and quick transitions but acknowledges difficulty in converting chances. Eritrea, with a 4-2-3-1, relies on defensive organization and counter-attacks, banking on Netabay's speed.

The match will be decisive for South Africa, who needs to maintain their lead, and for Eritrea, who seeks their first triumph in the group stage.

Broadcast and Lineups

The game will be broadcast by ESPN (BR) and can be followed live on the 365Scores platform. South Africa's probable lineup includes Ronwen Williams in goal, Moren, Makhanya, Sibisi, and Modiba in defense, and Mokoena, Bathusi Aubaas, and Zwane in midfield. For Eritrea, the probable formation features Sultan in goal, Fors, Misighna, Embaye, and Idris in defense, and Gerezgiher, Teklezghi (C), Yohannes, Netabay, Tekie, and Sulieman in attack.

Match Outcome Expectations

With South Africa leading the group and Mosimane's experience at Al Salam Stadium, the prediction points to a South African victory, although the clash could be hard-fought and goals might be scarce.
